kNN Classification

Source: vignettes/articles/r-docs/knn-classification.Rmd
knn-classification.Rmd

kNN Classification in R

Visualize k-Nearest Neighbors (kNN) classification in R with Plotly.

Basic binary classification with kNN

This section gets us started with displaying basic binary classification using 2D data. We first show how to display training versus testing data using various marker styles, then demonstrate how to evaluate our classifier’s performance on the test split using a continuous color gradient to indicate the model’s predicted score.

We will use the knn() function of the class package, which ships with R, to classify our data.

We will train a k-Nearest Neighbors (kNN) classifier. First, the model records the label of each training sample. Then, whenever we give it a new sample, it will look at the k closest samples from the training set to find the most common label, and assign it to our new sample. With prob = TRUE, knn() also returns the proportion of the k neighbours that voted for that label, which we use as the model’s score.

Display training and test splits

We first load synthetic data that form the shape of a moon. We then split it into a training and testing set. Finally, we display the ground truth labels using a scatter plot.

In the graph, we display all the negative labels as squares, and positive labels as circles. We differentiate the training and test set by adding a dot to the center of test data.

library(plotly.core)

make_moons <- read.csv(file = "data/make_moons.csv")
make_moons$y <- as.character(make_moons$y)
set.seed(123)
train_index <- sample(nrow(make_moons), 3/4 * nrow(make_moons))
make_moons$split <- "Test Split Label"
make_moons$split[train_index] <- "Train Split Label"
make_moons$label <- paste(make_moons$split, make_moons$y)

symbols <- c(
  "Train Split Label 0" = "square",
  "Train Split Label 1" = "circle",
  "Test Split Label 0" = "square-dot",
  "Test Split Label 1" = "circle-dot"
)

fig <- go_figure()
for (lab in names(symbols)) {
  fig <- fig |>
    add_scatter(
      data = make_moons[make_moons$label == lab, ],
      x = ~X1,
      y = ~X2,
      mode = "markers",
      name = lab,
      opacity = 0.5,
      marker = go_scatter_marker(
        symbol = symbols[[lab]],
        size = 12,
        color = "lightyellow",
        line = go_scatter_marker_line(color = "black", width = 1)
      )
    )
}

fig

Visualize predictions on test split

Now, we train the kNN model on the same training data displayed in the previous graph. Then, we predict the confidence score of the model for each of the data points in the test set. We will use shapes to denote the true labels, and the color will indicate the confidence of the model for assign that score.

Each label gets its own trace (and symbol), and both traces share the continuous color scale based on the yscore output by our kNN model.

library(plotly.core)
library(class)

make_moons <- read.csv(file = "data/make_moons.csv")
make_moons$y <- as.character(make_moons$y)
set.seed(123)
train_index <- sample(nrow(make_moons), 3/4 * nrow(make_moons))
make_moons$split <- "Test Split Label"
make_moons$split[train_index] <- "Train Split Label"

# kNN score: the fraction of the k nearest training samples labelled "1"
knn_score <- function(train, test, labels, k = 15) {
  pred <- knn(train, test, labels, k = k, prob = TRUE)
  ifelse(pred == "1", attr(pred, "prob"), 1 - attr(pred, "prob"))
}

train_data <- make_moons[make_moons$split == "Train Split Label", ]
pdb <- make_moons[make_moons$split == "Test Split Label", ]
pdb$yscore <- knn_score(
  train_data[, c("X1", "X2")],
  pdb[, c("X1", "X2")],
  train_data$y,
  k = 15
)

label_symbols <- c("0" = "square-dot", "1" = "circle-dot")

fig <- go_figure()
for (lab in names(label_symbols)) {
  fig <- fig |>
    add_scatter(
      data = pdb[pdb$y == lab, ],
      x = ~X1,
      y = ~X2,
      mode = "markers",
      name = lab,
      marker = go_scatter_marker(
        symbol = label_symbols[[lab]],
        size = 12,
        color = ~yscore,
        colorscale = "RdBu",
        cmin = 0,
        cmax = 1,
        showscale = lab == "1",
        colorbar = go_colorbar(title = "yscore"),
        line = go_scatter_marker_line(color = "black", width = 1)
      )
    )
}

fig

Probability Estimates with Contour

Just like the previous example, we will first train our kNN model on the training set.

Instead of predicting the confidence for the test set, we can predict the confidence map for the entire area that wraps around the dimensions of our dataset. To do this, we use meshgrid to create a grid, where the distance between each point is denoted by the mesh_size variable.

Then, for each of those points, we will use our model to give a confidence score, and plot it with a contour plot.

library(plotly.core)
library(pracma)
library(class)

make_moons <- read.csv(file = "data/make_moons.csv")
make_moons$y <- as.character(make_moons$y)
set.seed(123)
train_index <- sample(nrow(make_moons), 3/4 * nrow(make_moons))
make_moons$split <- "Test Split Label"
make_moons$split[train_index] <- "Train Split Label"

# kNN score: the fraction of the k nearest training samples labelled "1"
knn_score <- function(train, test, labels, k = 15) {
  pred <- knn(train, test, labels, k = k, prob = TRUE)
  ifelse(pred == "1", attr(pred, "prob"), 1 - attr(pred, "prob"))
}

mesh_size <- .02
margin <- 0.25
x_min <- min(make_moons$X1) - margin
x_max <- max(make_moons$X1) + margin
y_min <- min(make_moons$X2) - margin
y_max <- max(make_moons$X2) + margin
xrange <- seq(x_min, x_max, mesh_size)
yrange <- seq(y_min, y_max, mesh_size)
xy <- meshgrid(x = xrange, y = yrange)
xx <- xy$X
yy <- xy$Y

# score every point of the grid, using all the data points
final <- data.frame(X1 = as.vector(xx), X2 = as.vector(yy))
predicted <- knn_score(make_moons[, c("X1", "X2")], final, make_moons$y, k = 15)
Z <- matrix(predicted, nrow(xx), ncol(xx))

fig <- go_figure() |>
  add_contour(x = xrange, y = yrange, z = Z, colorscale = "RdBu")

fig

Now, let’s try to combine our Contour plot with the first scatter plot of our data points, so that we can visually compare the confidence of our model with the true labels.

library(plotly.core)
library(pracma)
library(class)

make_moons <- read.csv(file = "data/make_moons.csv")
make_moons$y <- as.character(make_moons$y)
set.seed(123)
train_index <- sample(nrow(make_moons), 3/4 * nrow(make_moons))
make_moons$split <- "Test Split Label"
make_moons$split[train_index] <- "Train Split Label"
make_moons$label <- paste(make_moons$split, make_moons$y)

# kNN score: the fraction of the k nearest training samples labelled "1"
knn_score <- function(train, test, labels, k = 15) {
  pred <- knn(train, test, labels, k = k, prob = TRUE)
  ifelse(pred == "1", attr(pred, "prob"), 1 - attr(pred, "prob"))
}

mesh_size <- .02
margin <- 0.25
x_min <- min(make_moons$X1) - margin
x_max <- max(make_moons$X1) + margin
y_min <- min(make_moons$X2) - margin
y_max <- max(make_moons$X2) + margin
xrange <- seq(x_min, x_max, mesh_size)
yrange <- seq(y_min, y_max, mesh_size)
xy <- meshgrid(x = xrange, y = yrange)
xx <- xy$X
yy <- xy$Y

# score every point of the grid, using all the data points
final <- data.frame(X1 = as.vector(xx), X2 = as.vector(yy))
predicted <- knn_score(make_moons[, c("X1", "X2")], final, make_moons$y, k = 15)
Z <- matrix(predicted, nrow(xx), ncol(xx))

symbols <- c(
  "Train Split Label 0" = "square",
  "Train Split Label 1" = "circle",
  "Test Split Label 0" = "square-dot",
  "Test Split Label 1" = "circle-dot"
)

fig <- go_figure() |>
  add_contour(x = xrange, y = yrange, z = Z, colorscale = "RdBu", opacity = 0.5)
for (lab in names(symbols)) {
  fig <- fig |>
    add_scatter(
      data = make_moons[make_moons$label == lab, ],
      x = ~X1,
      y = ~X2,
      mode = "markers",
      name = lab,
      marker = go_scatter_marker(
        symbol = symbols[[lab]],
        size = 12,
        color = "lightyellow",
        line = go_scatter_marker_line(color = "black", width = 1)
      )
    )
}

fig

Multi-class prediction confidence with Heatmap

It is also possible to visualize the prediction confidence of the model using heatmaps. In this example, you can see how to compute how confident the model is about its prediction at every point in the 2D grid. Here, we define the confidence as the difference between the highest score and the sum of the score of the other classes, at a certain point. Since the scores add up to 1, that is 2 * max_score - 1, where max_score is the proportion of neighbours that voted for the predicted class.

library(pracma)
library(plotly.core)
library(class)

data(iris) # We will use the iris data, which is included in R by default

mesh_size <- .02
margin <- 1

set.seed(123)
train_index <- sample(nrow(iris), 3/4 * nrow(iris))
train_data <- iris[train_index, ]
test_data <- iris[-train_index, ]

# Create a mesh grid on which we will run our model
l_min <- min(iris$Sepal.Length) - margin
l_max <- max(iris$Sepal.Length) + margin
w_min <- min(iris$Sepal.Width) - margin
w_max <- max(iris$Sepal.Width) + margin
lrange <- seq(l_min, l_max, mesh_size)
wrange <- seq(w_min, w_max, mesh_size)

mg <- meshgrid(lrange, wrange)
ll <- mg$X
ww <- mg$Y

# Run the classifier on the grid
final <- data.frame(Sepal.Length = as.vector(ll), Sepal.Width = as.vector(ww))
pred <- knn(
  train_data[, c("Sepal.Length", "Sepal.Width")],
  final,
  train_data$Species,
  k = 15,
  prob = TRUE
)

# Compute the classifier confidence
max_score <- matrix(attr(pred, "prob"), nrow(ll), ncol(ll))
diff <- 2 * max_score - 1

# Overlay the heatmap of the confidence on the scatter plot of the examples
species_symbols <- c(setosa = "square-dot", versicolor = "circle-dot", virginica = "diamond")

fig <- go_figure()
for (sp in names(species_symbols)) {
  fig <- fig |>
    add_scatter(
      data = test_data[test_data$Species == sp, ],
      x = ~Sepal.Length,
      y = ~Sepal.Width,
      mode = "markers",
      name = sp,
      marker = go_scatter_marker(
        symbol = species_symbols[[sp]],
        size = 12,
        color = "lightyellow",
        line = go_scatter_marker_line(width = 1.5)
      )
    )
}
fig <- fig |>
  add_heatmap(x = lrange, y = wrange, z = diff) |>
  update_layout(title = "Prediction Confidence on Test Split")

fig
